models.notes: Galbot G1 Chinese product page (Chinese labels translated in each conversion field). Workspace at the wrist centre: '垂直方向 0–2100 mm 水平方向 1900 mm' (vertical 0-2100 mm, horizontal 1900 mm), recorded as wrist-centre heights 0 to 2.1 m; the page does not name the floor, the workspace starting at 0 is read as the floor. Payload at the wrist centre: 5 kg per arm, 10 kg both. Arm length 710 mm from shoulder centre to wrist centre, recorded as reach (hand excluded). Max overall height 1730 mm; leg lift height difference 650 mm. Chassis 600 x 600 mm, projected circle 625 mm. 8 h working time; 3.5 h adapter charge. IP54. End effector exchangeable between dexterous hand, suction cup and gripper. DoF 21 excludes chassis and end effector. Page has 'Buy Now'.

models.notes: Dexmate Vega 1 Pro product page and 'Vega 1 Pro Full Spec Sheet' (PDF on the maker's CMS host). Maker's type: 'General-purpose wheeled humanoid'. Reach 'Floor to 7 ft 2 in (2.2 m)'; the page says 'A 3-DoF torso lifts the arms up to 7 ft 2 in (2.2 m) high'; which point of the hand the height refers to is not stated. Payload 5 kg per arm; the page adds 'in any pose'. Footprint is the folded envelope (L x W x H 0.66 x 0.56 x 0.66 m); the operating footprint is not stated; the page says folded it 'fits through a standard doorway'. Max height arms raised 2.50 m. Runtime 20 h. Omnidirectional base (2 steering, 2 drive). End effectors ordered separately (DexGripper S/D or third-party). Sold 'as a robot platform for developers and researchers'.

models.notes: Galaxea R1 series shop page, R1 Pro column ('R1 Pro 7-DOF Dual-Arm Wheeled Humanoid Robot'). Reach is 'Gripper-Equipped Arm Radius'. Payload per arm: rated 3.5 kg, maximum 5 kg. Vertical workspace 0-2000 mm, recorded as hand heights 0 to 2.0 m: the page does not name the floor, the workspace starting at 0 is read as the floor. 7-DoF arms, 4-DoF torso, 6-DoF omnidirectional chassis. Force-controlled parallel gripper, gripping range 0-100 mm, length 145 mm. Price $69,999.00, but the page also says: 'This product is not currently available for direct purchase from Galaxea Dynamics. For business or education purchases and enquiries, please contact product@galaxea-dynamics.com'. The cheaper R1 Lite ($39,999: 1281 × 596 × 670 mm, 96 kg, 6-DoF arms, arm radius 600 mm, rated 3 kg, vertical workspace 0-1700 mm, 1.5 m/s) is on the same page and could be added the same way.

models.notes: Almond Axol product page ('From $10,999', 'In stock', 'Ships from San Francisco'). Two 7-DoF arms; per arm: reach 860 mm, nominal payload 4 kg, peak payload 6.5 kg; repeatability 1 mm; weight 19.5 kg (standalone). The home page calls Axol 'a wheeled humanoid robot for physical AI', but the robot is sold standalone ('No base. Bolt Axol to your own table or fixture') with optional mounts: Owl Mount column, Ox Cart manual-lift cart, or Jelly Mobile powered base ('2.4 kWh battery, 610mm lift, and 1m/s drive'). Disagreement: the home page shows 'Lift680 mm' for Axol on Jelly vs '610mm lift' in the product text. Filed as a fixed dual arm on a table; an Axol-on-Jelly entry could be added as a wheeled humanoid with those base figures.
